rising.title: CoMeDA: an integrated platform for compositional analysis of metabarcoding data with batch correction
rising.title_zh: CoMeDA：一个用于 metabarcoding 数据组成分析并带批次校正的集成平台
rising.summary_zh: 摘要 背景 由 16S rRNA 和内部转录间隔区（ITS）扩增子测序产生的 metabarcoding 数据本质上是组成性的，观察到的丰度代表相对而非绝对信息。忽略这种组成结构可能导致下游分析中的虚假结果。此外，多队列研究经常遭受由样本处理或测序平台差异引起的批次效应，如果处理不当，可能混淆真实生物信号。尽管有多种微生物组分析平台可用，但这些分析考虑并不总是作为用户可访问工作流的核心组件整合在一起。结果 我们开发了 CoMeDA，一个集成网络平台，将 metabarcoding 数据的组成结构和批次效应作为单一分析工作流的协调组件处理。该平台支持原始 FASTQ 文件和预分类分类单元表，使其兼容短读长和长读长测序技术。CoMeDA 通过概率估计进行零值处理，并应用中心对数比（CLR）变换作为默认归一化策略，随后进行自动批次效应校正，去除技术变异同时保留生物信号。下游分析，包括使用组成适当

extra.description: Abstract Background Metabarcoding data generated from 16S rRNA and internal transcribed spacer (ITS) amplicon sequencing are inherently compositional, with observed abundances representing relative rather than absolute information. Ignoring this compositional structure can lead to spurious results in downstream analyses. In addition, multi-cohort studies frequently suffer from batch effects arising from differences in sample processing or sequencing platforms, which may confound true biological signals if not properly addressed. Despite the availability of multiple microbiome analysis platforms, these analytical considerations are not always incorporated together as central components of user-accessible workflows. Results We developed CoMeDA, an integrated web-based platform that treats the compositional structure of metabarcoding data and batch effects as coordinated components of a single analytical workflow. The platform supports both raw FASTQ files and pre-classified taxa tables, making it compatible with both short-read and long-read sequencing technologies. CoMeDA performs zero handling through probabilistic estimation and applies centered log-ratio (CLR) transformation as the default normalization strategy, followed by automated batch effect correction that removes technical variation while preserving biological signals. Downstream analyses, comprising diversity assessment using compositionally appropriate metrics, differential abundance analysis with effect size estimation, co-occurrence network inference, and functional prediction for both bacterial and fungal communities, are performed within the same compositional framework. CoMeDA also implements split-CLR transformation for cross-dataset analyses, enabling cross-kingdom and paired-condition correlation analyses while reducing spurious correlations introduced by directly combining datasets with different compositional structures. Using simulated datasets and a mock community with known ground truth, we evaluated the contribution of individual analytical components, the behavior of the automated batch-correction strategy, and taxonomic classification accuracy. We further reanalyzed a published multi-cohort gout dataset, a pediatric Crohn’s disease bacterial-fungal dataset, and a PacBio long-read periodontitis dataset. Using these datasets, CoMeDA recovered biologically coherent patterns while also highlighting additional literature-supported findings across different study designs. Conclusions CoMeDA provides a compositionally coherent workflow in which normalization, batch correction, and downstream analysis follow a consistent analytical logic. The platform features an interactive web interface and requires no programming expertise. CoMeDA is freely available online without registration, and a standalone Docker image is provided for local deployment.

new_today.title: Integration of polygenic risk with single cell methylation data using met-scDRS.
new_today.title_zh: 使用met-scDRS将多基因风险与单细胞甲基化数据整合。
new_today.summary_zh: 尽管大规模全基因组关联研究（GWAS）已识别出许多精神疾病性状的风险变异，但其功能含义仍 largely 未知。其风险的潜在机制之一是通过细胞背景依赖性表观遗传学如甲基化。先前方法侧重于将GWAS与单细胞转录组学整合，从而能够识别疾病风险关联的细胞类型内异质性。我们将此框架扩展为一种名为met-scDRS的方法，将GWAS与单细胞表观基因组学整合，并研究精神疾病风险如何通过单细胞分辨率的甲基化组学体现。我们提出一种方法，将单细胞甲基化组与GWAS识别的疾病相关基因在单细胞分辨率下整合。我们发现我们的方法在不同场景下校准良好且具有功效。然后我们分析了公开可用的人脑单细胞甲基化组数据集中的75种不同性状，并为每种性状的每个细胞生成疾病相关性评分。我们发现高脑特异性，主要细胞类型富集与已知发现一致。我们识别了沿大脑空间轴的精神疾病风险的细胞类型内异质性以及与疾病差异相关的亚群。最后，我们表明甲基

extra.description: Although large scale genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified many risk variants for psychiatric traits their functional implication remain largely unknown. One potential mechanism for their risk is through cellular context-dependent epigenetics such as methylation. Previous methodologies have focused on integrating GWAS with single cell transcriptomics, which allowed identification of within-cell-type heterogeneity in disease risk association. We extended this framework to provide a method called met-scDRS that integrates GWAS with single cell epigenomics and investigates how psychiatric disease risk can manifest through methylomics at single cell resolution. We propose an approach that integrates single cell methylomes with disease associated genes identified from GWAS at single-cell resolution. We found our method to be well calibrated and powered in different scenarios. We then analyzed a publicly available single cell methylome dataset of the human brain for 75 different traits and generated disease relevance scores for each cell for each trait. We find high brain specificity with major cell type enrichments congruent with known findings. We identify within-cell-type heterogeneity for psychiatric disease risk along the brain spatial axis as well as subpopulations that are differentially associated with diseases. Finally, we showed that genes with high correlation between methylation levels and disease relevance scores to be highly enriched in specific functional pathways such as synaptic formation and transmission. met-scDRS is freely available in GitHub as a python package under MIT license: https://github.com/bogdanlab/met-scDRS. Source code is also available from Zenodo with DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.21841506. All dataset used in this work are publicly available. Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

new_today.title: HRD: an integrated multi-omics resource for human reproduction and development
new_today.title_zh: HRD：人类生殖与发育的综合多组学资源
new_today.summary_zh: 摘要 人类生殖与发育是一个由遗传、分子和环境因素塑造的连续过程。然而，相关数据仍分散在公共存储库和文献中，限制了系统整合、分析和再利用。我们开发了人类生殖与发育数据库（HRD；http://www.inbirg.com/hrd/），这是一个综合多组学资源，组织与多个生殖、妊娠和发育背景相关的公开可用数据。HRD 1.0版包含814条组学记录，包括432条批量转录组、144条单细胞或单核转录组、156条表观基因组、52条代谢组和30条蛋白质组记录，以及702条临床试验记录、293条暴露-结局关联和779个带有 curated 表型关联的先导SNP。通过协调关键元数据并应用数据类型特定的分析工作流，HRD将组学数据、遗传关联、暴露-结局证据和临床试验数据纳入一个共同框架，以探索生殖和发育多个阶段的数据。该网站支持关键词搜索、组合筛选、基于类别的浏览、统计摘要和数据下载，并提供差异分析、功能富集

extra.description: Abstract Human reproduction and development span a continuum shaped by genetic, molecular, and environmental factors. However, relevant data remain dispersed across public repositories and the literature, limiting systematic integration, analysis, and reuse. We developed the Human Reproduction and Development Database (HRD; http://www.inbirg.com/hrd/), an integrated multi-omics resource that organizes publicly available data relevant to multiple reproductive, pregnancy, and developmental contexts. HRD version 1.0 contains 814 omics records, including 432 bulk transcriptomic, 144 single-cell or single-nucleus transcriptomic, 156 epigenomic, 52 metabolomic, and 30 proteomic records, together with 702 clinical trial records, 293 exposure-outcome associations, and 779 lead SNPs with curated phenotype associations. By harmonising key metadata and applying data-type-specific analysis workflows, HRD brings omics data, genetic associations, exposure-outcome evidence, and clinical trial data into a common framework for exploring data from multiple stages of reproduction and development. The website supports keyword search, combined filtering, category-based browsing, statistical summaries and data downloads, and provides interactive visualizations of differential analyses, functional enrichment, cell clustering, chromatin accessibility, peak annotation, regulatory networks, and cross-phenotype association plots. HRD supports the retrieval, comparison, and reuse of reproductive and developmental data and analysis results.

dropped.title_zh: 一种用于稀有细胞感知单细胞RNA-seq数据生成的图注意力GAN
dropped.summary_zh: 单细胞RNA测序（scRNA-seq）下游分析的一个核心挑战是高维小样本（HDSS）情形，且常因稀有细胞类型而加剧类别不平衡。这些因素阻碍了稳健的特征（基因）选择和细胞聚类，并限制了现有模拟器生成样本的真实性。我们提出GARAGE，一种图注意力稀有细胞感知单细胞数据生成方法，在先验噪声之外，用少量、注意力加权的真实细胞“泄漏”来增强生成器输入。具体来说，我们构建k近邻细胞图，并使用图注意力网络（GAT）优先选择可能代表欠采样（稀有）亚群的节点；这些高注意力细胞嵌入被注入生成器输入，以引导合成朝向数据流形中生物学上合理的区域，同时尊重细胞类型比例。这种注意力引导泄漏加速训练，减少模式丢失，并生成保留稀有细胞结构的真实合成细胞。在真实scRNA-seq基准上，GARAGE相比最先进基线改善了下游特征选择和聚类。总之，GARAGE通过将图注意力与对抗生成结合，直接应对scRNA-seq中的HDS

extra.description: A central challenge in downstream single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) analysis is the high-dimensional, small-sample (HDSS) regime, often compounded by class imbalance from rare cell types. These factors hinder robust feature (gene) selection and cell clustering and limit the realism of samples generated by existing simulators. We introduce GARAGE , a G raph- A ttentive RA re-cell aware single-cell data GE neration that augments the generator’s input with a small, attention-weighted ‘leakage’ of real cells in addition to prior noise. Specifically, we build a k -nearest-neighbour cell graph and use a graph attention network (GAT) to prioritize nodes that likely represent under-sampled (rare) subpopulations; these high-attention cell embeddings are injected into the generator input to steer synthesis toward biologically plausible regions of the data manifold while respecting cell-type proportions. This attention-guided leakage accelerates training, reduces mode dropping, and yields realistic synthetic cells that preserve rare-cell structure. Across real scRNA-seq benchmarks, GARAGE improves downstream feature selection and clustering compared with state-of-the-art baselines. In summary, GARAGE directly addresses HDSS and rarity in scRNA-seq by coupling graph attention with adversarial generation to produce high-fidelity synthetic cells that enhance downstream analyses. The corresponding software is available at: https://github.com/RitwikGanguly/GARAGE .

dropped.title_zh: HRD：一个面向人类生殖与发育的整合多组学资源。
dropped.summary_zh: 人类生殖与发育是一个由遗传、分子和环境因素塑造的连续过程。然而，相关数据仍分散在公共存储库和文献中，限制了系统性整合、分析和复用。我们开发了人类生殖与发育数据库（HRD；http://www.inbirg.com/hrd/），这是一个整合多组学资源，用于组织与多种生殖、妊娠和发育情境相关的公开可用数据。HRD 1.0版包含814条组学记录，包括432条bulk转录组、144条单细胞或单核转录组、156条表观基因组、52条代谢组和30条蛋白质组记录，以及702条临床试验记录、293条暴露-结局关联和779个带有 curated 表型关联的 lead SNP。通过协调关键元数据并应用数据类型特定的分析流程，HRD将组学数据、遗传关联、暴露-结局证据和临床试验数据纳入一个共同框架，用于探索生殖与发育多个阶段的数据。该网站支持关键词搜索、组合筛选、基于类别的浏览、统计摘要和数据下载，并提供差异分析

extra.description: Human reproduction and development span a continuum shaped by genetic, molecular, and environmental factors. However, relevant data remain dispersed across public repositories and the literature, limiting systematic integration, analysis, and reuse. We developed the Human Reproduction and Development Database (HRD; http://www.inbirg.com/hrd/), an integrated multi-omics resource that organizes publicly available data relevant to multiple reproductive, pregnancy, and developmental contexts. HRD version 1.0 contains 814 omics records, including 432 bulk transcriptomic, 144 single-cell or single-nucleus transcriptomic, 156 epigenomic, 52 metabolomic, and 30 proteomic records, together with 702 clinical trial records, 293 exposure-outcome associations, and 779 lead SNPs with curated phenotype associations. By harmonising key metadata and applying data-type-specific analysis workflows, HRD brings omics data, genetic associations, exposure-outcome evidence, and clinical trial data into a common framework for exploring data from multiple stages of reproduction and development. The website supports keyword search, combined filtering, category-based browsing, statistical summaries and data downloads, and provides interactive visualizations of differential analyses, functional enrichment, cell clustering, chromatin accessibility, peak annotation, regulatory networks, and cross-phenotype association plots. HRD supports the retrieval, comparison, and reuse of reproductive and developmental data and analysis results.

extra.description: Abstract Cancer subtype classification based on molecular features is important for characterizing tumor heterogeneity, evaluating patient prognosis, and supporting precision treatment. Multi-omics integration provides complementary molecular information across genomic, epigenomic, transcriptomic, and proteomic levels. However, the high dimensionality of multi-omics data, complex cross-omics relationships, and imbalanced subtype distributions remain major challenges. To address these issues, we propose CALT-GNN, a graph neural network framework that integrates patient-similarity graph learning, cross-attention-based omics integration, long-tail expert classification, and learnable prediction fusion. The framework first constructs omics-specific patient-similarity graphs, learns latent patient representations using graph convolutional networks, and obtains a unified graph through similarity network fusion. A cross-attention branch models complementary relationships between CNA and DNA methylation as source modalities and mRNA expression as the target modality. In parallel, a long-tail expert branch uses Major and Minor Experts with prototype-guided routing to perform class-distribution-aware classification. The outputs of the two branches are subsequently combined using a learnable global weight. Experiments on eight TCGA multi-omics cohorts showed that CALT-GNN achieved competitive or comparable classification performance relative to representative baseline methods and stable performance on Macro-F1 and MCC, which are sensitive to class imbalance. Ablation and subtype-level analyses further supported the complementary contributions of cross-omics interaction modeling and adaptive long-tail expert routing, although the magnitude of the improvements varied across cohorts and subtypes. These results suggest that CALT-GNN provides a methodological framework for multi-omics cancer subtype classification under complex cross-omics relationships and imbalanced subtype distributions.

extra.description: Abstract Background Mapping spatially coherent tissue domains from spatial transcriptomics data is a prerequisite for characterizing cell-type, developmental patterning, and disease-associated disruptions of tissue architecture. While graph neural network (GNN) methods have substantially improved domain identification over expression-only clustering, the effect of edge feature design (i.e. how spatial connections between tissue spots are represented) has never been systematically evaluated. All existing methods use a single scalar edge weight, leaving open the question of whether multi-dimensional edge features provide any benefit. Methods We introduce RMGAT, a Relational Multi-Scale Graph Attention Network that applies multi-dimensional learned edge features to spatial transcriptomics, to the best of our knowledge for the first time. Each spatial edge is described by an 8-dimensional learned feature vector. We combine this with a three-component training objective (graph reconstruction, NT-Xent contrastive learning, and a self-expression decoder) and a V30 post-processing pipeline using consensus clustering, Hungarian label alignment, and spatial refinement. Results Evaluated on the 12-section DLPFC (human dorsolateral prefrontal cortex) benchmark across 60 independent runs (5 seeds × 12 DLPFC sections), RMGAT achieves a mean adjusted Rand index (ARI) of 0.3422 ± 0.0402 (95% confidence interval [0.332, 0.353]), comparable to SpaGCN (~ 0.36). A systematic four-component ablation study with formal statistical testing identifies GAT attention as the only statistically confirmed essential contributor (ΔARI = − 0.028 when replaced with a graph convolutional network, GCN; p < 0.0001). Contrastive learning shows a directional benefit (ΔARI = − 0.017; p = 0.024 vs. scalar-weight baseline). The 8-dimensional EdgeMLP and self-expression decoder are both neutral (ΔARI ≈ 0.004; both p > 0.3), indicating neither contributes at PCA-50 input quality. Conclusions The primary contribution of this work is a systematic ablation study providing evidence-based design guidance for spatial transcriptomics GNNs. At PCA-50 input quality, GAT attention is the statistically confirmed critical component; contrastive learning is beneficial ( p = 0.024); multi-dimensional edge features and additional decoder objectives do not improve performance under this input regime. For practitioners, these findings support using GAT attention ( p < 0.0001) and contrastive learning ( p = 0.024, non-significant after Bonferroni correction), and investing in node feature quality over edge feature complexity.

longest_on_board.title: 基于多智能体深度强化学习的SD-IoT控制器部署
longest_on_board.title_zh: 基于多智能体深度强化学习的SD-IoT控制器部署
longest_on_board.summary_zh: 物联网(IoT)中激增的流量, 影响了传感器等设备的数据传输。利用软件定义网络(SDN)技术可以优化网络性能, 提高数据传输质量。然而, 物联网中流量等网络状态的不断变化会影响软件定义网络控制平面的性能。研究软件定义物联网(SD-IoT)中的动态控制器部署问题, 以在流量变化时保证控制平面性能。考虑到物联网节点的能耗以及数据传输的特点, 在部署控制器时, 综合考虑延迟、控制可靠性以及能耗的影响, 并将该问题构建为马尔可夫博弈过程。为了同时兼顾单一控制器性能以及控制平面整体性能, 采用多智能体深度强化学习求解该问题。在部署阶段利用动作掩码屏蔽部分节点, 避免将控制器部署在性能不足或者供能不方便的节点。仿真实验表明, 与基于Louvain社区划分和基于单智能体深度Q网络(DQN)的部署算法相比, 所提算法可以更好地找到高性能的部署方案。

longest_on_board.summary_zh: 在高速收费站拥堵检测场景中, 遮挡、阴影、景深等因素严重影响检测算法的精度, 基于单信息的拥堵检测算法无法准确反映收费站真实拥堵情况, 对此, 提出一种高速收费站多信息融合拥堵检测算法。首先采用目标检测算法检测目标区域车辆, 利用图像空间特征计算车道占用率; 其次利用Deep SORT目标跟踪算法与滑动平衡机制进行车流量综合估计, 减少因为遮挡和阴影导致的车辆误检、漏检问题; 最后利用基于光流信息熵的车速估计方法, 降低因景深变化导致的拥堵状态检测误差。通过融合3种不同维度信息得到拥堵指数, 拥堵指数聚类为5种拥堵类别以判断真实拥堵状态, 从而实现高速收费站的拥堵检测。实验结果表明, 在高速收费站拥堵数据集上, 采用多信息融合的拥堵检测算法准确率达到90.4%, 能够实现对收费站拥堵状态的准确检测。
